cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Recruit Them Twice
cards.instruction: Recruit them to your side, then reveal that the side, goal, or conflict is not what it first appeared to be.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I signed where you signed. Now help me save the club garden.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Gladly, but I signed the extension plan. It builds over half the garden.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, getting inside the proposal. We'll start by withdrawing both our signatures.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I paid for the planning drawings myself. I don't want that money wasted.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then help me find a use for those drawings that keeps the garden. You're joining the redesign, not the building campaign.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies a planning signature without its purpose; A3 claims insider strategy and asks reversal; A5 uses B4 personal drawing expense to recruit B into redesign instead of supporting construction.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 lost garden area gives A3 signature withdrawal; B4 paid drawings gives A5 a salvage goal that preserves the garden.

relationship.evidence: B4 has a concrete financial reason to resist undoing the proposal.

heightening.evidence: A5 changes what joining means again because B4 needs its expenditure to retain value.

specificity.evidence: A1 signature, B2 half-garden footprint and B4 personally funded drawings make the political and financial conflict explicit.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 redesign-not-building names the actual work requested, not an abstract explanation of recruitment.
